claims.text: OrderService's constructor takes IOrderRepository and INotifier; PlaceOrderAsync throws on an empty items list, sets Status "new", calls repository.AddAsync and SaveChangesAsync, sends "order placed" through notifier.Send, and returns the order.
OrderPlacedTightlyCoupled initialises a private readonly EmailNotifier field with new() and Handle calls notifier.Send(orderId, "order placed").
NotifierBase.Send formats the message, adds it to a private list exposed as the read-only Sent property, and writes it with Console.WriteLine; EmailNotifier inherits from NotifierBase.
OrderNotifications takes an INotifier constructor parameter, so a caller can pass an EmailNotifier it created and read its Sent list after calling Handle.
DonHang.Tests constructs OrderService directly with two in-memory classes implementing IOrderRepository and INotifier and checks PlaceOrderAsync without a database.
Any code can construct OrderService with new and its own IOrderRepository/INotifier; the container is not required.

claims.text: A class built around injected abstractions can be checked in isolation; one that creates its own dependencies can only be checked together with what they really do, unless it is edited.
Placing an order through the API needs a signed-in customer (OrdersController.Create has [Authorize]), an HTTP request and PostgreSQL, and each successful call leaves an order row.
Checking PlaceOrderAsync with in-memory stand-ins needs no PostgreSQL, leaves no row behind, and runs in milliseconds.
